# Physical Agent Architecture {.unnumbered}

\chapter*{Part II: Physical Agent Architecture}

In modern computer science, an artificial intelligence agent is commonly conceptualized as a language model in a loop: it reads text prompts, maintains memory context, reasons about sub-goals, calls software tools or APIs, and returns an output.

In Physical AI, the agentic flow follows the same cognitive lifecycle (perception, memory, reasoning, planning, and execution), but every step must translate across the physical boundary where software moves matter, inertia carries mass, and time cannot be paused.


## The Core Systems Tension: High-Capacity Learned Models vs. Deterministic Real-Time Control

In Part I, we established the immutable physical and temporal laws of embodied systems and traced the cognitive workflow. That foundational analysis revealed the core paradox of Physical AI: physics demands immediate action, while cognition demands time to deliberate.

A physical AI machine cannot be a single, monolithic neural network running on a cloud server. It is an integrated physiological system comprising five distinct sensory-motor organs operating across different temporal rates, silicon fabrics, and trust boundaries:

![**The Embodied Sensory-Motor Dataflow and Inter-Stage Contracts.** The complete architectural progression across Part II. Each sensory-motor organ executes an internal transformation (the intra-stage dataflow) and formalizes its verified output into an engineering contract that feeds the subsequent stage (the inter-stage dataflow), closing the loop through physical actuation.](figures/fig_part2_dataflow.svg){#fig-part2-dataflow width=100%}

### The Two Complementary Dataflows of Embodied Systems

To engineer this multi-rate architecture without race conditions or physical instability, we must understand two complementary flows of information:

1. **The Intra-Stage Dataflow (Within the Organ):** How raw data enters the physical substrate, traverses silicon buses, gets transformed by modern foundation models, and gets bounded by physical dynamics inside a single chapter.
2. **The Inter-Stage Dataflow (Across the Sensory-Motor Loop):** How the structured output of one stage becomes the foundational input of the next stage across the closed loop:

* **@sec-perception: Perception and Spatial Encoders (Raw Photons $\to$ 3D Tokens $O_t$):** Transforms continuous physical photon fluxes into compact 3D Spatial Affordance Tokens ($O_t \in SE(3)$) on edge neural accelerators, formalizing the **Spatial Affordance Interface (OBS-01)**.
* **@sec-state: Memory and Latent World Models (3D Tokens $O_t \to$ World Belief $S_t$):** Integrates instantaneous, occlusion-prone tokens into persistent $SE(3)$ kinematic frame trees and latent predictive world models, formalizing the **World State Belief Interface (STATE-01)**.
* **@sec-intent: Intent and Reasoners (World Belief $S_t \to$ Intent Lease $\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}$):** Grounds high-level human instructions into 3D geometric bounding boxes as an untrusted System 2 proposal service on application processors, formalizing the **Expiring Intent Lease Interface (INTENT-01)**.
* **@sec-planning: Planning and Trajectory Synthesis (Intent Lease $\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}} \to$ Action Chunks $\tau_t$):** Unrolls semantic goals into $H$-step continuous trajectory chunks smoothed with quintic polynomial splines to bound mechanical jerk ($\|\dddot{\mathbf{q}}\| \le j_{\text{max}}$), formalizing the **Trajectory Chunking Interface (PLAN-01)**.
* **@sec-enforcement: Reflexes and Safety Enforcement (Action Chunks $\tau_t \to$ Permitted Motor Voltages $u_t^*$):** Enforces hard forward-invariance Control Barrier Functions ($h(x) \ge 0$) and dynamic stopping envelopes ($d_{\text{stop}} \le d_{\text{clearance}}$) on isolated bare-metal microcontrollers, formalizing the **Safety Enforcement Interface (SAFE-01)**.

Part II resolves the tension between computation and physical dynamics by systematically constructing, isolating, and validating each of these five sensory-motor organs across the proposal and permission boundary.
